A truly new recipe therefore already enters the new-system ingestion pipeline at creation and should be reviewed via ordinary /mapping-review, never batch-remediated — batch remediation exists only for the pre-Implementation-6 backlog (Group A).

alreadyRemediatedRecipes.rationale: All three used the real reviewer contract, real admin-verified persistence, and a real admin decision-maker; the end-to-end validation audit records no fabricated votes or invented provenance. projectedFullRemediationWorkload_LABELED.projectedUnionCandidatesFormula: 226 recipes * 18.76 avg union candidates/recipe (measured full-228-corpus average)
projectedFullRemediationWorkload_LABELED.caveat: These are projections extrapolated from a 36-recipe frozen benchmark and a full-228-corpus reviewer-union average, not a measurement of the current 226-recipe population. No human review time-per-item estimate is provided — the repository contains no authoritative seconds/minutes-per-relationship data.

batchSizeOptionsConsidered.note: Smallest failure-isolation blast radius; too many batches (46) for 226 recipes, high per-batch operational overhead.
Fewer batches (12) but a single batch could carry ~280 projected review items at the measured rate, a large single review session with more to lose per failed batch.

batching.rationale: 10 recipes/batch caps nominal AI calls at 20/batch (bounded max 40 with full retry), keeps projected review burden per batch to roughly 100 relationships (~10 recipes * 14.09/affected-recipe * ~94% affected), matches the pilot-size guidance (5-10) so the pilot itself can double as a template batch, and gives 23 batches for the 226 fresh-generation recipes after the pilot consumes 5 of them — small enough per batch to stop cleanly on a systemic problem without losing much sunk work.

maxConcurrentRecipeGenerations.rationale: No existing batch-orchestration harness runs multiple /api/mapping/generate calls concurrently in this repo; sequential-by-recipe during the pilot maximizes auditability and failure attribution. Once the pilot validates the mechanism, bounded concurrency of up to 3 recipe generations in flight keeps total in-flight reviewer calls to at most 6 (2 reviewer slots x 3 recipes) — well below any provider concern raised in prior sessions, without assuming unlimited concurrency.

batching.reviewerConcurrencyNote: Unchanged from the existing implemented coordinator: each recipe's own 2 reviewer slots (A and B) already execute independently per the review-routing contract Sec 6; this plan does not alter that.
batching.generationVsReviewSequencing: SEQUENTIAL_PER_BATCH — generate every recipe in a batch first (bounded concurrency), then perform human review for the whole batch, then completeness review/attest/approve for the whole batch, before starting the next batch's generation. Recommended for the pilot and initial batches to favor operational simplicity and clean stop points; pipelining batch N+1 generation during batch N's review may be revisited once the pilot proves the workflow, but is not adopted now.

batchOrdering.method: Descending known-severity first: rank Group A's 226 fresh-generation-eligible recipes by the 2026-08-26 completeness audit's per-recipe false-negative (FN) count (highest first), assign consecutively to batches of 10 in that order. The exact 226-row ranked list is not hand-enumerated in this plan (the audit JSON is 5.3MB); Prompt C should derive it programmatically from docs/audits/cooking-mode-completeness-audit-2026-08-26.json's per-recipe FN counts at execution time, filtered to Group A's fresh-generation set.
batchOrdering.rejectedAlternative: Round-robin distribution of severity ranks across batches (to smooth review burden per batch) was considered and rejected in favor of the simpler descending-severity ordering, which front-loads risk reduction and early validation value as instructed; revisit only if a specific batch's review burden proves unmanageable in practice.

proposalReuseRules: Before generating: compute the recipe's current recipeRevision from its live parsed content.
If a current-approved pointer resolves CURRENT for that exact revision -> skip remediation entirely (Group B pattern).
Else if a READY proposal exists at that exact revision -> reuse it; resume/continue human review from its existing state (grilled-zucchini-and-summer-squash pattern).

Else if a WRITING or FAILED proposal header exists at that identity -> do not trust it; fall through and generate fresh (per architecture contract Sec 27.1 step 2 - this is already the implemented behavior of generateAndPersistCookingModeMappingProposal, not new logic this plan invents).
Else -> generate fresh (standard Group A case, 226 recipes).
batchStatusLifecycleNote: Planning-level/audit-ledger states only, tracked in external remediation-run ledger artifacts (one JSON per batch run). Not a new persisted production lifecycle field — the actual per-recipe/per-proposal state remains exactly the existing MappingProposalStatus/queue-derived states the persistence layer and /mapping-review UI already compute.
revisionFreeze: Before generating a batch recipe, record its recipeRevision. At review/attestation/approval time, the existing contract already re-verifies recipeRevision server-side (addHumanMappingRelationship, recordMappingCompletenessAttestation, and the approve route all re-derive/compare live revision - Sec 26.4, 26.6, 27.3). If a source change is detected, the old proposal becomes stale by the existing STALE pointer classification (Sec 25.6); the recipe leaves the current batch and re-enters a later remediation cycle as a fresh-generation case.
v4v5Preservation: No code path in this plan writes recipe.cookingStepIngredientMap or any other v4/v5 runtime field. All remediation writes are confined to recipes/{id}/mappingProposals/**, approvedMappings/**, and cookingModeMappingPointer/current - the same subcollections the 2026-08-29 end-to-end validation confirmed are fully isolated from Cooking Mode runtime reads (components/CookingMode.tsx and app/recipes/[id]/page.tsx have zero references to the new paths).

fullCorpusQualityGates.source: docs/architecture/cooking-mode-review-routing-contract.md Sec 23 (Activation gates) and docs/audits/cooking-mode-mapping-architecture-reassessment-2026-08-28.md - unchanged, not lowered by this planning task.
fullCorpusQualityGates.preparedComponentGate: Separate, not defined by this task (Sec 21 of the contract defers prepared components entirely; V10A arbiter precision was ~40.49%).

migrationManifestContract.immutabilityRequirement: Manifest is immutable once approved - no edit-in-place; a correction requires a new manifest version.

shaLock.method: canonical fixed-key-order JSON serialization of the full manifest, then SHA-256
shaLock.requirement: Production apply must require the exact expected manifest hash as a precondition; apply performs zero AI calls, zero mapping recomputation, zero candidate rerouting, and zero review decisions - a purely deterministic manifestation of already-approved truth, following the same pattern the existing v4/v5 apply scripts (scripts/apply-cooking-step-mapping-v4-core.mjs, scripts/apply-recovered-recipe-mapping-v5-core.mjs) already demonstrate in this repository.

optionA_pointerDirect.description: Cooking Mode reads cookingModeMappingPointer/current -> approvedMappings/{mapId} directly at request time.

tradeoffs.runtimeSimplicity: Lower - adds a new read path alongside the existing recipe fetch/cache; components/CookingMode.tsx and app/recipes/[id]/page.tsx need new code.
tradeoffs.readCount: At least 2 additional reads per recipe view (pointer + approved map) unless denormalized/cached.
tradeoffs.offlineBehavior: Unclear without denormalization into the already-cached recipe document; needs verification against the existing recipe cache/offline behavior.
tradeoffs.migrationRisk: Lower - no shared-document field mutation; the recipe document itself is never touched.
tradeoffs.rollbackBehavior: Simplest possible - stop reading the pointer path; old v4/v5 field was never touched, so no data rollback is needed.
tradeoffs.iosSharedBackendCompatibility: Not a constraint per PRD.md Sec 1/Known Sharp Edges - 'the deprecated iOS client is not a compatibility constraint.'
tradeoffs.existingCodeChurn: Higher - new runtime read path in Cooking Mode's hot path.

optionB_materialize.description: Production apply writes the approved relationships back onto the existing recipe.cookingStepIngredientMap field (a new engineVersion/schema variant), reusing the exact field Cooking Mode already validates and safely falls back from.

tradeoffs.runtimeSimplicity: Higher - zero Cooking Mode/runtime code changes; the exact same validated-field-with-safe-fallback path already in production today.
tradeoffs.readCount: Unchanged - one recipe document read, as today.
tradeoffs.migrationRisk: Higher - this is a real mutation to the shared recipe document, which is exactly what the SHA-locked manifest/apply architecture (Sec 20-21 of this plan) exists to make safe.
tradeoffs.rollbackBehavior: Requires restoring the prior field value/hash captured pre-cutover in the manifest's oldRuntimeMap* fields - a real data rollback, but one the manifest is explicitly designed to carry.
tradeoffs.existingCodeChurn: Lower - reuses the proven field-only-write-with-SHA-lock-and-precondition pattern this repo's existing v4/v5 apply tooling already implements.

cutoverOptions.recommendedApproach: Option B (materialize onto the existing cookingStepIngredientMap field) - tentative preference, not a final decision. Reuses an already-implemented, already-audited operational pattern (SHA-locked field-only apply) in this exact repository, requires zero Cooking Mode runtime code changes, and keeps read/offline/cache behavior completely unchanged. Option A remains architecturally cleaner (never mutates the shared recipe document) and should be reconsidered if a future requirement needs multiple concurrently-valid maps per recipe or a non-recipe-document read path.
cutoverOptions.unresolvedImplications: iOS/shared-backend compatibility is NOT an open question - PRD.md is explicit that the deprecated iOS client is not a compatibility constraint. The remaining open question for the cutover task is purely about Cooking Mode web runtime code shape (Option A vs B) and should be explicitly reconfirmed, not silently inherited from this tentative recommendation, before implementation begins.

requirements: Old v4/v5 map value and its own sourceHash/engineVersion must be captured verbatim in the manifest's oldRuntimeMap* fields before any apply, even if that value is 'field absent' for the 7 unresolved/1 malformed exclusions.
Pre-cutover value/hash must be captured for every recipe in the applied batch.
New approved map remains immutable regardless of rollback (the approvedMappings collection is never deleted or edited).
Manifest records both old and new state so a reverse-manifest can be constructed without re-deriving anything.
rollbackPlan.rollbackMeaning: Depends on the eventual cutover option: under Option B, rollback means restoring the old materialized cookingStepIngredientMap field value from the manifest's captured pre-cutover snapshot (a real, field-only, SHA-locked reverse write). Under Option A, rollback means simply repointing/disabling the new runtime read path back to the old field, since the old field was never mutated.
rollbackPlan.aiInvolvement: Zero - rollback never calls AI, recomputes nothing, and only replays already-captured values.

operationalNotes: The /mapping-review queue is a flat unfiltered list (loadMappingReviewQueue - a bounded unfiltered collection-group scan, no composite index) - adequate for the pilot (8 recipes) and default batch size (10 recipes) but has no batch-grouping, sort-by-severity, or progress-across-batches view.

No blocker is raised because remediation batches are small (<=10 recipes) and short-lived - an admin can track batch membership externally via the remediation ledger (Sec 14) rather than needing new product UI.

If batch size or corpus cadence later increases substantially (e.g. running many batches per day, or wanting an in-app 'batch N of M' view), revisit this as a possible small UX enhancement then - not now, to avoid feature creep.

executionPromptSequence.name: Pilot corpus remediation
executionPromptSequence.scope: Generate proposals for the 5 fresh-generation pilot recipes; resume review for grilled-zucchini-and-summer-squash; reconfirm garlic-butter-herb-steak-bites-with-potatoes and caprese-salad pointers CURRENT. Review/attest/approve all 8. No migration. Produce a remediation ledger for this pilot run.

executionPromptSequence.name: Pilot validation
executionPromptSequence.scope: Measure the pilot's actual review burden, quality (spot-check against completeness-audit adjudicated values), and operational results against the Pilot Gate criteria in this plan. Decide GO/NO-GO for remaining corpus.

executionPromptSequence.name: Remaining corpus generation/review
executionPromptSequence.scope: Execute the remaining ~23 bounded batches of <=10 recipes each (221 recipes) in descending-severity order, using the batch statuses in this plan. Potentially repeated across multiple sessions.

executionPromptSequence.name: Full approved-corpus quality validation
executionPromptSequence.scope: Measure precision/recall/severity-class recall of the complete approved-map population against the full-corpus quality gates (Sec 19 of the architecture plan). No runtime cutover.

executionPromptSequence.name: Build immutable migration manifest
executionPromptSequence.scope: Construct and SHA-lock the migration manifest per the contract in this plan, for the in-scope approved population only.

executionPromptSequence.name: Production apply/cutover
executionPromptSequence.scope: Execute the deterministic, zero-AI, zero-recomputation manifest apply. Requires the cutover-option architecture decision (Sec 22/this plan) to be explicitly confirmed first.

executionPromptSequence.name: Post-cutover production verification
executionPromptSequence.scope: Confirm Cooking Mode runtime reads the new source of truth correctly, with rollback evidence in hand.

stopConditions: Reviewer transport/schema failure rate rises above what the existing bounded per-slot retry (2 attempts/slot) absorbs cleanly across a batch
A systematic false-positive pattern appears in more than one pilot/batch recipe's approved map
A systematic critical-omission pattern (a whole class of ingredient use consistently missed) appears across recipes
Review burden per recipe is substantially worse than the 14.09-items/affected-recipe modeled estimate across a full batch
The /mapping-review UI becomes operationally unusable at the batch scale actually observed (contradicting the Sec 25/this-plan sufficiency assessment)
Source/parser corruption is discovered beyond the already-known cases (chipotle-tahini-bowls, mole-poblano)
A CANDIDATE_ID_COLLISION or persistence identity conflict occurs
An unexpected Firestore scaling/composite-index requirement surfaces
preparedComponentBoundary: Explicitly out of scope for this plan and for the entire ingredient-mapping remediation effort. Ingredient-mapping remediation must not wait for prepared-component quality to improve (current V10A arbiter precision ~40.49%, per docs/audits/cooking-mode-mapping-architecture-reassessment-2026-08-28.md) unless a specific recipe's Cooking Mode correctness is found to actually require a prepared-component relationship - no such requirement has been identified in this planning task.
